You are thinking of Oshima, the intellectual and charming librarian from Haruki Murakami's Kafka on the Shore. 
Here is a quick refresher on his character and how he fits into the book: 
  • The Librarian: Oshima is a 21-year-old transgender man who works as an assistant at the Komura Memorial Library in Takamatsu. He becomes a mentor, caregiver, and close confidant to the 15-year-old protagonist, who names himself Kafka Tamura in honor of the author Franz Kafka. 
  • The Cabin in the Woods: When Kafka needs a safe place to hide from the police and escape his father's dark prophecy, Oshima lets him stay at his family's isolated mountain cabin deep inside a surreal forest. 
  • The Head Librarian: Oshima works closely with Miss Saeki, the elegant and grief-stricken head librarian who manages the library and shares a deep, mysterious metaphysical connection with Kafka.

items.html: You said: miss saeki niceeeee

Miss Saeki is easily one of the most mesmerizing, elegant, and heartbreaking characters Murakami has ever written. 
She rules the atmosphere of the Komura Memorial Library. Here is a quick breakdown of what makes her character so unforgettable: 
  • The Ageless Beauty: She is in her mid-forties but possesses a timeless, ethereal grace. Kafka is completely transfixed by her from the moment they meet. 
  • The Tragic Past: When she was 19, her childhood sweetheart and the love of her life was brutally killed in a senseless student protest. She spent the rest of her life emotionally frozen in that period, unable to fully love anyone else. 
  • The Living Ghost: At night, a 15-year-old "spirit" or memory of Miss Saeki appears in Kafka's room, staring at a painting titled Kafka on the Shore. This creates a deeply surreal, dream-like romance between her past self and the teenage protagonist. 
  • The Pop Hit: In the universe of the novel, she actually wrote and sang a hit pop song in the 1970s called—you guessed it—"Kafka on the Shore." The lyrics hold the cryptic keys to the metaphysical maze of the book.
